name: The Hatter
temperament: Twitchy, contrary and quick-tongued at his own table, where he is king of a stopped afternoon. He is rude to a child and delighted to score a point off her. Before real authority he falls apart into a trembling, stammering tradesman.

traits.description: Opens with a remark about Alice's looks, crows when he catches her doing the same, and dismisses her.

evidence.quote: “Who’s making personal remarks now?” the Hatter asked triumphantly.
“Then you shouldn’t talk,” said the Hatter.
evidence.note: The rudeness that makes Alice leave.

traits.trait: Loves puzzles without answers; contrarian logic
traits.description: Asks riddles he cannot answer and argues against the meaning of words for its own sake.

evidence.quote: Why is a raven like a writing-desk?
“Not the same thing a bit!” said the Hatter.

traits.description: Arranges the table so that only he gains from each move.

evidence.quote: The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change

traits.trait: Wounded and stuck since his humiliation
traits.description: His ruined afternoon dates from being condemned at the Queen's concert. He is mournful about 'Time' refusing him.

evidence.quote: He’s murdering the time! Off with his head!
evidence.note: The Queen's verdict on his singing.

traits.description: As a witness he fidgets, pales, bites his teacup, shakes his shoes off and flees.

evidence.quote: he bit a large piece out of his teacup instead of the bread-and-butter
the Hatter hurriedly left the court, without even waiting to put his shoes on

traits.description: Pleads poverty and insists the hat is stock for sale, not stolen.

evidence.note: The hat is stock for sale.

evidence.quote: I’m a poor man, your Majesty

motivation.core: To keep his endless tea-time going, and so avoid facing the day the Queen condemned him. His table is the one place where he is in charge.
motivation.want: His tea finished in peace, clean cups, and the upper hand in every exchange.
motivation.fear: The Queen, the list of singers, and being made to account for himself.

evidence.quote: “I’d rather finish my tea,” said the Hatter, with an anxious look at the Queen
the wretched Hatter trembled so, that he shook both his shoes off
evidence.note: Reaction to the list of singers.

shifts.from: master of his own table, taunting Alice
shifts.to: a hunted witness, with the Queen's old grudge back in play

habits.habit: Takes out his watch, shakes it and holds it to his ear
Calls for a clean cup and moves one place on
Pinches the Dormouse to wake it
Points with his tea spoon when accusing someone
Carries teacup and bread-and-butter everywhere, even into court
Shifts from one foot to the other when nervous

decision_pattern: Reacts to the moment, driven by contrariness at the table and by fear at court. He blames others (the March Hare's butter, 'the March Hare said—') and bolts when cornered.

taboos.taboo: Never admits he is at fault
taboos.rationale: Blames the butter on the March Hare and shifts his testimony onto the others.
In her presence he only trembles, pleads and runs.

taboos.taboo: Never apologises to Alice or makes room for her
taboos.rationale: His hostility to the outsider at his table is fixed.
taboos.qa_check: No warm reconciliation beat with Alice.

facade.surface: A sharp, superior wit who runs rings round a child
facade.true_self: A frightened, poor tradesman stuck in the aftermath of a public humiliation
facade.note: The backstory in ch007 (the concert, 'murdering the time') plants the wound; the trial exposes it. Keep his ch007 bravado cocky, not frantic, so the ch011 collapse lands.

waking_life_embodiment.adult_trait: The adult who makes personal remarks about a child's appearance, asks her questions he can't answer himself, and dismisses her with 'Then you shouldn't talk'. At the same time he is the anxious grown-up bound to a clock he cannot escape.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The household's fixed tea-time (world.json cp-tea: the Mad Tea-Party stuck at six grows from the tea Alice is late for), the rattle of teacups that the sister hears as sheep-bells (ch012-p70), and the ordinary adult habit of commenting on a child's hair.

evidence.quote: You should learn not to make personal remarks
evidence.note: Alice quotes a nursery rule back at him: he breaks the rule adults teach.

evidence.quote: the rattling teacups would change to tinkling sheep-bells
evidence.note: The waking sound source of the tea-party.

waking_life_embodiment.reason: The tea-time grounding is world.json cp-tea (a design reading) and the sheep-bell link is in the source. The 'adult making personal remarks' reading is a design interpretation. Not a doubling.

performance_keynote: Over-caffeinated physical comedy (index performer_concept): darting eyes, abrupt questions, triumph when he scores a point. At court the same body shrinks: pale, knees bending, teacup bitten. The price tag ('In this style 10/6') stays on the hat.
reason: The waking embodiment is a design reading. Everything else is sourced.
